sanskrit: tathā bruvantaṃ tam ahaṃ rāmaṃ parapuraṃjayam naitad evaṃ punar bhāvi brahmarṣe kiṃ śrameṇa te
english: To Rāma, conqueror of hostile cities, as he spoke thus, I replied: "This shall not come to pass, O brahmin-sage; why do you trouble yourself?"

sanskrit: gurutvaṃ tvayi saṃprekṣya jāmadagnya purātanam prasādaye tvāṃ bhagavaṃs tyaktaiṣā hi purā mayā
english: Looking upon your ancient standing as my teacher, O son of Jamadagni, I seek your favor, O blessed one; for she was renounced by me long ago.

sanskrit: ko jātu parabhāvāṃ hi nārīṃ vyālīm iva sthitām vāsayeta gṛhe jānan strīṇāṃ doṣān mahātyayān
english: For who, knowing the grievous faults that ruin women, would ever house a woman whose heart belongs to another, one who dwells like a serpent within his home?

sanskrit: na bhayād vāsavasyāpi dharmaṃ jahyāṃ mahādyute prasīda mā vā yad vā te kāryaṃ tat kuru māciram
english: Not even out of fear of Vāsava would I abandon my duty, O greatly radiant one. Be gracious, or else do without delay whatever you intend.

sanskrit: ayaṃ cāpi viśuddhātman purāṇe śrūyate vibho maruttena mahābuddhe gītaḥ śloko mahātmanā
english: And this verse too, O pure-souled and mighty lord, is heard in the ancient lore, sung by the great-minded, great-souled Marutta:

sanskrit: guror apy avaliptasya kāryākāryam ajānataḥ utpathapratipannasya kāryaṃ bhavati śāsanam
english: "Even a teacher who is arrogant, who knows not right action from wrong, who has strayed onto a crooked path—him it is proper to chastise."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ gurur iti premṇā mayā saṃmānito bhṛśam guruvṛttaṃ na jānīṣe tasmād yotsyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: You, deemed my teacher, I have honored exceedingly out of affection; yet you know not the conduct befitting a teacher—therefore I shall fight with you.

sanskrit: guruṃ na hanyāṃ samare brāhmaṇaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ viśeṣatas tapovṛddham evaṃ kṣāntaṃ mayā tava
english: I would not slay a teacher in battle, and least of all a brahmin, and most of all one grown great in austerity—thus have I borne with you.

sanskrit: udyateṣum atho dṛṣṭvā brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatrabandhuvat yo hanyāt samare kruddho yudhyantam apalāyinam brahmahatyā na tasya syād iti dharmeṣu niścayaḥ
english: But when a brahmin, like a kinsman of the warrior caste, is seen with arrow drawn, whoever in wrath should slay him in battle as he fights and does not flee—upon him no guilt of brahmin-slaughter falls: such is the settled rule in the sacred laws.

sanskrit: kṣatriyāṇāṃ sthito dharme kṣatriyo 'smi tapodhana yo yathā vartate yasmiṃs tathā tasmin pravartayan nādharmaṃ samavāpnoti naraḥ śreyaś ca vindati
english: I am a kṣatriya, abiding in the duty of kṣatriyas, O you whose wealth is penance. The man who deals with another just as that other deals with him incurs no unrighteousness and attains what is best.

sanskrit: arthe vā yadi vā dharme samartho deśakālavit anarthasaṃśayāpannaḥ śreyān niḥsaṃśayena ca
english: He who is competent in matters of gain or of duty, who knows place and time, even when fallen into doubt and adversity, fares better than one who acts without due reflection.

sanskrit: yasmāt saṃśayite 'rthe 'smin yathānyāyaṃ pravartase tasmād yotsyāmi sahitas tvayā rāma mahāhave paśya me bāhuvīryaṃ ca vikramaṃ cātimānuṣam
english: Since in this doubtful matter you proceed according to your own notion of justice, therefore I shall join battle with you, Rāma, in this great fight. Behold the might of my arms and my more-than-human valor.

sanskrit: evaṃ gate 'pi tu mayā yac chakyaṃ bhṛgunandana tat kariṣye kurukṣetre yotsye vipra tvayā saha dvaṃdve rāma yatheṣṭaṃ te sajjo bhava mahāmune
english: Even with things come to this pass, O delight of the Bhṛgus, I shall do what lies in my power. On Kurukṣetra I shall fight with you, O brahmin; in single combat, Rāma, as you wish—make ready, O great sage.

sanskrit: tatra tvaṃ nihato rāma mayā śaraśatācitaḥ lapsyase nirjitāṃl lokāñ śastrapūto mahāraṇe
english: There, Rāma, slain by me and bristling with a hundred shafts, purified by weapons in that great battle, you shall win the worlds you have conquered.

sanskrit: sa gaccha vinivartasva kurukṣetraṃ raṇapriya tatraiṣyāmi mahābāho yuddhāya tvāṃ tapodhana
english: So go now, turn back toward Kurukṣetra, O lover of battle. There I shall come to you for combat, O mighty-armed one whose wealth is penance.

sanskrit: api yatra tvayā rāma kṛtaṃ śaucaṃ purā pituḥ tatrāham api hatvā tvāṃ śaucaṃ kartāsmi bhārgava
english: And in that very place where once, Rāma, you performed the purifying rite for your father, there too, having slain you, I shall perform the purifying rite, O Bhārgava.

sanskrit: tatra gacchasva rāma tvaṃ tvaritaṃ yuddhadurmada vyapaneṣyāmi te darpaṃ paurāṇaṃ brāhmaṇabruva
english: Go there, Rāma, in haste, O you maddened for battle; I shall strip away your old pride, you who are a brahmin but in name.

sanskrit: yac cāpi katthase rāma bahuśaḥ pariṣatsu vai nirjitāḥ kṣatriyā loke mayaikeneti tac chṛṇu
english: And as for your repeated boast in assemblies, Rāma—'By me alone were the kṣatriyas of the world subdued'—hear now my answer to that.

sanskrit: na tadā jāyate bhīṣmo madvidhaḥ kṣatriyo 'pi vā yas te yuddhamayaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ ca vyapanāśayet
english: In those days there was born no Bhīṣma, nor any kṣatriya of my measure, who could have destroyed your battle-pride and your desire.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ jāto mahābāho bhīṣmaḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ vyapaneṣyāmi te darpaṃ yuddhe rāma na saṃśayaḥ
english: But now that Bhīṣma is born, O mighty-armed one, conqueror of hostile cities—I shall undo your pride in battle, Rāma, of that there is no doubt.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato mām abravīd rāmaḥ prahasann iva bhārata diṣṭyā bhīṣma mayā sārdhaṃ yoddhum icchasi saṃgare
english: Bhīṣma said: Then Rāma, as if laughing, said to me, O Bhārata: "By good fortune, Bhīṣma, you wish to do battle with me in the field."

sanskrit: ayaṃ gacchāmi kauravya kurukṣetraṃ tvayā saha bhāṣitaṃ tat kariṣyāmi tatrāgaccheḥ paraṃtapa
english: "Here I go, O Kaurava, to Kurukṣetra together with you; I shall make good my word. Come there, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: tatra tvāṃ nihataṃ mātā mayā śaraśatācitam jāhnavī paśyatāṃ bhīṣma gṛdhrakaṅkabaḍāśanam
english: "There may your mother Jāhnavī behold you slain by me, Bhīṣma, bristling with a hundred shafts, made food for vultures, herons, and crows."

sanskrit: kṛpaṇaṃ tvām abhiprekṣya siddhacāraṇasevitā mayā vinihataṃ devī rodatām adya pārthiva
english: "Gazing piteously upon you slain by me, let the goddess, attended by Siddhas and Cāraṇas, weep this day, O prince."

sanskrit: atadarhā mahābhāgā bhagīrathasutā nadī yā tvām ajījanan mandaṃ yuddhakāmukam āturam
english: "Undeserving of such grief is that blessed river, daughter of Bhagīratha, who bore you—a fool, sick with the lust for war."

sanskrit: ehi gaccha mayā bhīṣma yuddham adyaiva vartatām gṛhāṇa sarvaṃ kauravya rathādi bharatarṣabha
english: "Come, go with me, Bhīṣma; let the battle take place this very day. Take up all your gear—chariot and the rest—O Kaurava, bull of the Bharatas."

sanskrit: iti bruvāṇaṃ tam ahaṃ rāmaṃ parapuraṃjayam praṇamya śirasā rājann evam astv ity athābruvam
english: To Rāma, conqueror of hostile cities, as he spoke thus, I bowed my head, O king, and said, "So be it."

sanskrit: evam uktvā yayau rāmaḥ kurukṣetraṃ yuyutsayā praviśya nagaraṃ cāhaṃ satyavatyai nyavedayam
english: Having said this, Rāma set off for Kurukṣetra eager to fight; and I, entering the city, made it known to Satyavatī.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtasvastyayano mātrā pratyabhinanditaḥ dvijātīn vācya puṇyāhaṃ svasti caiva mahādyute
english: Then, the rites of blessing performed and welcomed by my mother, having had the twice-born pronounce the auspicious day and the benediction, O greatly radiant one—

sanskrit: ratham āsthāya ruciraṃ rājataṃ pāṇḍurair hayaiḥ sūpaskaraṃ svadhiṣṭhānaṃ vaiyāghraparivāraṇam
english: —mounting a gleaming silver chariot drawn by white horses, well equipped, sturdily framed, draped about with tiger-skins,

sanskrit: upapannaṃ mahāśastraiḥ sarvopakaraṇānvitam tat kulīnena vīreṇa hayaśāstravidā nṛpa
english: furnished with great weapons and provided with every appurtenance, O king—that chariot, with a hero of noble birth, learned in the science of horses,

sanskrit: yuktaṃ sūtena śiṣṭena bahuśo dṛṣṭakarmaṇā daṃśitaḥ pāṇḍureṇāhaṃ kavacena vapuṣmatā
english: yoked with a well-bred charioteer many times proven in action—I, mailed in white armor that lent splendor to my frame,

sanskrit: pāṇḍuraṃ kārmukaṃ gṛhya prāyāṃ bharatasattama pāṇḍureṇātapatreṇa dhriyamāṇena mūrdhani
english: taking up a white bow, set forth, O best of the Bharatas, with a white parasol held above my head,

sanskrit: pāṇḍuraiś cāmaraiś cāpi vījyamāno narādhipa śuklavāsāḥ sitoṣṇīṣaḥ sarvaśuklavibhūṣaṇaḥ
english: fanned with white yak-tail whisks, O lord of men, clad in white, turbaned in white, adorned with ornaments all of white,

sanskrit: stūyamāno jayāśīrbhir niṣkramya gajasāhvayāt kurukṣetraṃ raṇakṣetram upāyāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: hymned with blessings of victory, I went forth from the City named for the Elephant and came to Kurukṣetra, the field of battle, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: te hayāś coditās tena sūtena paramāhave avahan māṃ bhṛśaṃ rājan manomārutaraṃhasaḥ
english: Urged on by that charioteer toward the great fight, those horses, swift as thought and wind, bore me swiftly onward, O king.

sanskrit: gatvāhaṃ tat kurukṣetraṃ sa ca rāmaḥ pratāpavān yuddhāya sahasā rājan parākrāntau parasparam
english: Having reached Kurukṣetra, both I and the valorous Rāma at once advanced against each other for combat, O king.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdarśane 'tiṣṭhaṃ rāmasyātitapasvinaḥ pragṛhya śaṅkhapravaraṃ tataḥ prādhamam uttamam
english: Then I took my stand within sight of Rāma, that supreme ascetic, and taking up my finest conch, I blew upon it a mighty blast.

sanskrit: tatas tatra dvijā rājaṃs tāpasāś ca vanaukasaḥ apaśyanta raṇaṃ divyaṃ devāḥ sarṣigaṇās tadā
english: Then, O king, the twice-born and the ascetics dwelling in the forest, and the gods with their hosts of seers, looked on at that wondrous combat.

sanskrit: tato divyāni mālyāni prādurāsan muhur muhuḥ vāditrāṇi ca divyāni meghavṛndāni caiva ha
english: Then again and again heavenly garlands appeared, and heavenly music sounded, and gathered banks of cloud.

sanskrit: tatas te tāpasāḥ sarve bhārgavasyānuyāyinaḥ prekṣakāḥ samapadyanta parivārya raṇājiram
english: Then all those ascetics, the followers of the Bhārgava, became onlookers, ringing about the field of battle.

sanskrit: tato mām abravīd devī sarvabhūtahitaiṣiṇī mātā svarūpiṇī rājan kim idaṃ te cikīrṣitam
english: Then the goddess, my mother, who seeks the welfare of all beings, appearing in her own form, said to me, O king: "What is this you intend to do?"

sanskrit: gatvāhaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ taṃ prayāciṣye kurūdvaha bhīṣmeṇa saha mā yotsīḥ śiṣyeṇeti punaḥ punaḥ
english: "I shall go to the son of Jamadagni and entreat him, O upholder of the Kurus, again and again: 'Do not fight with Bhīṣma, who is your pupil.'"

sanskrit: mā maivaṃ putra nirbandhaṃ kuru vipreṇa pārthiva jāmadagnyena samare yoddhum ity avabhartsayat
english: "Do not, do not, my son, persist thus in fighting in battle with a brahmin, the son of Jamadagni"—so she reproached me.

sanskrit: kiṃ na vai kṣatriyaharo haratulyaparākramaḥ viditaḥ putra rāmas te yatas tvaṃ yoddhum icchasi
english: "Is not Rāma known to you, my son—the slayer of kṣatriyas, whose valor equals Hara's—that you wish to do battle with him?"

sanskrit: tato 'ham abruvaṃ devīm abhivādya kṛtāñjaliḥ sarvaṃ tad bharataśreṣṭha yathāvṛttaṃ svayaṃvare
english: Then, saluting the goddess with joined palms, I told her all, O best of the Bharatas—everything that had befallen at the bride-choosing,

sanskrit: yathā ca rāmo rājendra mayā pūrvaṃ prasāditaḥ kāśirājasutāyāś ca yathā kāmaḥ purātanaḥ
english: and how Rāma had earlier been entreated by me, O king of kings, and what the long-standing desire of the daughter of the king of Kāśi had been.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā rāmam abhyetya jananī me mahānadī madarthaṃ tam ṛṣiṃ devī kṣamayām āsa bhārgavam bhīṣmeṇa saha mā yotsīḥ śiṣyeṇeti vaco 'bravīt
english: Then my mother, the great river-goddess, went up to Rāma and for my sake sought to appease that seer, the Bhārgava, saying, "Do not fight with Bhīṣma, who is your pupil."

sanskrit: sa ca tām āha yācantīṃ bhīṣmam eva nivartaya na hi me kurute kāmam ity ahaṃ tam upāgamam
english: But he said to her as she pleaded, "Turn Bhīṣma back instead, for he will not do my will"—and so I came up against him.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato gaṅgā sutasnehād bhīṣmaṃ punar upāgamat na cāsyāḥ so 'karod vākyaṃ krodhaparyākulekṣaṇaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Gaṅgā, out of love for her son, approached Bhīṣma once more; but he, his eyes troubled with wrath, would not heed her word.

sanskrit: athādṛśyata dharmātmā bhṛguśreṣṭho mahātapāḥ āhvayām āsa ca punar yuddhāya dvijasattamaḥ
english: Then the righteous one, foremost of the Bhṛgus, great in austerity, came into view, and that best of the twice-born once again summoned him to battle.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tam ahaṃ smayann iva raṇe pratyabhāṣaṃ vyavasthitam bhūmiṣṭhaṃ notsahe yoddhuṃ bhavantaṃ ratham āsthitaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: As he stood ready in the field, I answered him, smiling, as it were: "Standing on the ground, I cannot bring myself to fight you while I am mounted upon a chariot."

sanskrit: āroha syandanaṃ vīra kavacaṃ ca mahābhuja badhāna samare rāma yadi yoddhuṃ mayecchasi
english: "Mount a chariot, O hero, and gird on armor, O mighty-armed Rāma, if you wish to do battle with me in the field."

sanskrit: tato mām abravīd rāmaḥ smayamāno raṇājire ratho me medinī bhīṣma vāhā vedāḥ sadaśvavat
english: Then Rāma said to me, smiling on the field of battle: "The earth is my chariot, Bhīṣma; the Vedas are my horses, like fine steeds."

sanskrit: sūto me mātariśvā vai kavacaṃ vedamātaraḥ susaṃvīto raṇe tābhir yotsye 'haṃ kurunandana
english: "The Wind is my charioteer, and the mothers of the Vedas are my armor; well sheathed in these, I shall fight in the field, O delight of the Kurus."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇo gāndhāre rāmo māṃ satyavikramaḥ śaravrātena mahatā sarvataḥ paryavārayat
english: Speaking thus, O Gāndhāra, Rāma of unfailing valor enveloped me on every side with a vast multitude of arrows.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ rathe divye vyavasthitam sarvāyudhadhare śrīmaty adbhutopamadarśane
english: Then I beheld the son of Jamadagni stationed upon a heavenly chariot, bearing every weapon, splendid, of a wondrous aspect beyond compare,

sanskrit: manasā vihite puṇye vistīrṇe nagaropame divyāśvayuji saṃnaddhe kāñcanena vibhūṣite
english: fashioned by thought, holy, spacious as a city, yoked with heavenly steeds, fully arrayed and adorned with gold,

sanskrit: dhvajena ca mahābāho somālaṃkṛtalakṣmaṇā dhanurdharo baddhatūṇo baddhagodhāṅgulitravān
english: and with a banner, O mighty-armed one, marked by the emblem of the moon. A bowman, his quiver bound on, his lizard-skin guard and finger-guards fastened—

sanskrit: sārathyaṃ kṛtavāṃs tatra yuyutsor akṛtavraṇaḥ sakhā vedavid atyantaṃ dayito bhārgavasya ha
english: and there Akṛtavraṇa, the friend of the Bhārgava, knower of the Vedas and exceedingly dear to him, served as charioteer for the warrior eager to fight.

sanskrit: āhvayānaḥ sa māṃ yuddhe mano harṣayatīva me punaḥ punar abhikrośann abhiyāhīti bhārgavaḥ
english: As he summoned me to battle, the Bhārgava seemed to gladden my heart, crying out again and again, "Come on, advance!"

sanskrit: tam ādityam ivodyantam anādhṛṣyaṃ mahābalam kṣatriyāntakaraṃ rāmam ekam ekaḥ samāsadam
english: That Rāma—like the rising sun, unassailable, of mighty strength, the ender of the kṣatriyas—I, alone, advanced upon, alone.

sanskrit: tato 'haṃ bāṇapāteṣu triṣu vāhān nigṛhya vai avatīrya dhanur nyasya padātir ṛṣisattamam
english: Then, at a distance of three arrow-falls, I reined in my horses, and descending and laying aside my bow, I went on foot toward that best of seers,

sanskrit: abhyagacchaṃ tadā rāmam arciṣyan dvijasattamam abhivādya cainaṃ vidhivad abruvaṃ vākyam uttamam
english: approaching Rāma, that best of the twice-born, to do him honor; and saluting him in due form, I spoke these noble words:

sanskrit: yotsye tvayā raṇe rāma viśiṣṭenādhikena ca guruṇā dharmaśīlena jayam āśāssva me vibho
english: "I shall fight with you in battle, Rāma—with one greater and superior, a teacher of righteous conduct. Wish me victory, O lord."

sanskrit: rāma uvāca evam etat kuruśreṣṭha kartavyaṃ bhūtim icchatā dharmo hy eṣa mahābāho viśiṣṭaiḥ saha yudhyatām
english: Rāma said: "Even so it is, O best of the Kurus; thus should one act who desires prosperity. For this is the duty, O mighty-armed one, of those who fight with their superiors."

sanskrit: śapeyaṃ tvāṃ na ced evam āgacchethā viśāṃ pate yudhyasva tvaṃ raṇe yatto dhairyam ālambya kaurava
english: "I would have cursed you had you not come thus, O lord of the people. Fight on, then, in the field, intent and steadfast, O Kaurava."

sanskrit: na tu te jayam āśāse tvāṃ hi jetum ahaṃ sthitaḥ gaccha yudhyasva dharmeṇa prīto 'smi caritena te
english: "Yet I do not wish you victory, for I am here to conquer you. Go, fight by the rule of righteousness; I am pleased with your conduct."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato 'haṃ taṃ namaskṛtya ratham āruhya satvaraḥ prādhmāpayaṃ raṇe śaṅkhaṃ punar hemavibhūṣitam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, bowing to him, I quickly mounted my chariot and once more blew upon my gold-adorned conch in the field.

sanskrit: tato yuddhaṃ samabhavan mama tasya ca bhārata divasān subahūn rājan parasparajigīṣayā
english: Then battle was joined between me and him, O Bhārata, for very many days, O king, each seeking to vanquish the other.

sanskrit: sa me tasmin raṇe pūrvaṃ prāharat kaṅkapatribhiḥ ṣaṣṭyā śataiś ca navabhiḥ śarāṇām agnivarcasām
english: In that combat he struck me first with shafts fledged with heron-feathers—nine hundred and sixty arrows blazing like fire.

sanskrit: catvāras tena me vāhāḥ sūtaś caiva viśāṃ pate pratiruddhās tathaivāhaṃ samare daṃśitaḥ sthitaḥ
english: By them my four horses and my charioteer too were checked, O lord of the people; yet I stood firm in the fray, clad in mail.

sanskrit: namaskṛtya ca devebhyo brāhmaṇebhyaś ca bhārata tam ahaṃ smayann iva raṇe pratyabhāṣaṃ vyavasthitam
english: And bowing to the gods and to the brahmins, O Bhārata, I answered him, smiling, as it were, as he stood ready in the field:

sanskrit: ācāryatā mānitā me nirmaryāde hy api tvayi bhūyas tu śṛṇu me brahman saṃpadaṃ dharmasaṃgrahe
english: "Your teacherhood has been honored by me, even though you have overstepped all bounds; yet hear from me further, O brahmin, what is fitting in the gathering of righteousness."

sanskrit: ye te vedāḥ śarīrasthā brāhmaṇyaṃ yac ca te mahat tapaś ca sumahat taptaṃ na tebhyaḥ praharāmy aham
english: "The Vedas that dwell within your body, your great brahmin-hood, and the mighty austerity you have practiced—at these I do not strike."

sanskrit: prahare kṣatradharmasya yaṃ tvaṃ rāma samāsthitaḥ brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyatvaṃ hi yāti śastrasamudyamāt
english: "I strike at the warrior's office, which you, Rāma, have assumed; for a brahmin passes into the state of a kṣatriya by the lifting of weapons."

sanskrit: paśya me dhanuṣo vīryaṃ paśya bāhvor balaṃ ca me eṣa te kārmukaṃ vīra dvidhā kurmi sasāyakam
english: "Behold the prowess of my bow, behold the strength of my arms. Lo, hero, I split your bow in two, arrow and all."

sanskrit: tasyāhaṃ niśitaṃ bhallaṃ prāhiṇvaṃ bharatarṣabha tenāsya dhanuṣaḥ koṭiś chinnā bhūmim athāgamat
english: I let fly at him a sharp broad-headed shaft, O bull of the Bharatas; by it the tip of his bow was severed and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: nava cāpi pṛṣatkānāṃ śatāni nataparvaṇām prāhiṇvaṃ kaṅkapatrāṇāṃ jāmadagnyarathaṃ prati
english: And nine hundred arrows, straight-jointed and fledged with heron-feathers, I sent flying at the chariot of the son of Jamadagni.

sanskrit: kāye viṣaktās tu tadā vāyunābhisamīritāḥ celuḥ kṣaranto rudhiraṃ nāgā iva ca te śarāḥ
english: Lodged then in his body and stirred by the wind, those arrows quivered, dripping blood, like serpents.
